name: momentum_reversion_switch_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY/BANKNIFTY, intraday sessions alternate between two microstructure states: (1) directional flow, where large institutional TWAP/VWAP algorithms push the index with sustained order imbalance visible as ADX > 25 on a 5-minute window — in this state, a 1.5-minute EMA crossing above a 3.5-minute EMA signals order-flow acceleration already underway, predicting 15-25 more spot points of continuation within 30-60 seconds; and (2) range-bound churning, where market makers are net-flat and delta-hedging activity creates tight oscillations — ADX < 18 identifies this state, and 2-sigma Bollinger Band extremes on a 5-minute window flag overshoots that market makers fade within 30 seconds, recovering 10-20 spot points back toward the band midline. The switching logic is the unique edge: a pure momentum strategy bleeds in low-ADX chop, and a pure reversion strategy is crushed in trending regimes — the classifier prevents each sub-strategy from trading in its hostile environment.

indicators.name: adx_60
indicators.purpose: 60-bar (5-minute) ADX is the regime classifier, not a trade trigger — so it can and should be longer than the hold time. 5 minutes is enough context on NIFTY to reliably distinguish trending (institutional TWAP flow) from choppy (market-maker recycling) behavior. Shorter ADX (e.g., 1-2 min) would flip too fast and mis-classify. Longer (10+ min) would lag regime transitions. 5 min is the canonical NIFTY microstructure regime window.

indicators.name: ema_fast_18
indicators.purpose: 18 bars = 1.5 minutes. This is the TRADE TRIGGER in the trend regime — it must match the hold time (30-90s). A 1.5-min EMA crossing above the 3.5-min EMA signals that the most recent directional push has decisively overtaken the slightly-longer trend, indicating fresh institutional flow has just started. The original used EMA(9) on 1-min bars = 9 minutes of context; we compress to 1.5 min because our hold is 30-90s, not 15-60 min.

indicators.name: ema_slow_42
indicators.purpose: 42 bars = 3.5 minutes. Contextual anchor for EMA crossover. The original used EMA(21) on 1-min = 21 minutes. Scaled to 3.5 min because we want the slow EMA to represent the current session's short-term drift, not the multi-hour trend. The EMA_fast/EMA_slow ratio (1.5min/3.5min = same 2.3x ratio as 9/21) is preserved intentionally to maintain the relative relationship between the two EMAs.

indicators.name: vwap
indicators.purpose: No lookback needed — cumulative from 09:15. Used as directional filter: in the trend regime, we only take EMA crossovers in the direction of VWAP bias (bullish cross above VWAP = buy CE; bearish cross below VWAP = buy PE). In the reversion regime, VWAP confirms the overshoot is a fade candidate (price above BB_upper AND above VWAP → overextended, fade it).

indicators.name: bb_60_2sd
indicators.purpose: 60-bar (5-minute) Bollinger Bands. The reversion regime requires bands that capture the current session's volatility range — 5 min is long enough to define a stable range and short enough to stay current with intraday regime changes. 2σ threshold corresponds to a ~5% probability event on a normal distribution, meaning the index has moved sharply enough that market makers are actively fading it. Original used BB(20) on 1-min = 20 minutes; compressed to 5 min because our reversion play targets only the first 30-60 seconds of the bounce, not the full recovery.

conditions: MOMENTUM REGIME: adx_60 > 25 AND ema_fast_18 crosses above ema_slow_42 AND close > vwap
REVERSION REGIME: adx_60 < 18 AND close < bb_lower AND close < vwap
buy_ce.confirmation: Both conditions checked simultaneously — no additional bar confirmation needed at 5s resolution (adding a bar adds 5s lag which kills the entry)

conditions: MOMENTUM REGIME: adx_60 > 25 AND ema_fast_18 crosses below ema_slow_42 AND close < vwap
REVERSION REGIME: adx_60 < 18 AND close > bb_upper AND close > vwap

exit.stop_rationale: Momentum regime stop: 4 pts = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. If an EMA crossover fails and the index retraces 8 spot points within 30s, the institutional flow thesis is wrong and the position is abandoned. Reversion regime stop: 3 pts = ~6 spot points. A BB overshoot that deepens by another 6 spot points is not reverting — it is breaking out — and must be exited before further damage.
exit.target_rationale: Momentum target: 7 pts = ~14 spot points. NIFTY momentum continuations after EMA crossovers in a trending regime typically run 15-25 spot points in 30-60s; targeting 14 captures roughly 60% of the median move (1:1.75 R:R). Reversion target: 5 pts = ~10 spot points. BB mean-reversion bounces in low-ADX NIFTY typically recover 10-20 spot points back toward the band midline; targeting 10 is conservative at the lower bound (1:1.67 R:R).

filters.vix_filter: None — strategy is self-classifying via ADX; VIX regime overlap adds noise without benefit
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:20 (pre-open noise) or after 15:20 IST (EOD risk)
filters.volume_filter: None at index level — NIFTY/BANKNIFTY volume is always sufficient
filters.trend_filter: ADX threshold IS the trend filter — intrinsic to strategy logic
filters.spread_filter: Not applicable — limit orders at candle close prices
filters.dead_zone_filter: ADX 18-25 is the 'dead zone' — neither sub-strategy fires, position is flat

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — ADX regime classification is widely known; but combining it with distinct sub-strategies that have opposite entry logic creates a structural barrier to replication. Pure momentum players and pure reversion players cannot replicate this without a classifier.

adaptation_notes: Major changes from original: (1) Universe removed — original traded NIFTY50 constituent stocks filtered by ADV/beta; now trades NIFTY index directly. The regime-switching thesis is actually STRONGER on the index because institutional flow is more predictable and less noisy at index level. (2) Timeframes compressed by ~10x: ADX(14 × 1-min) → ADX(60 × 5s) = 5 min; EMA(9,21 × 1-min) → EMA(18,42 × 5s) = 1.5/3.5 min; BB(20 × 1-min) → BB(60 × 5s) = 5 min. The EMA fast/slow ratio (2.3x) is preserved. (3) Hold time reduced from 15-60 min to 30-90 sec — we capture only the initial burst, not the sustained run. (4) Stops/targets converted from basis points (0.30-0.50%) to option premium points. (5) Volume filter dropped — not meaningful on index. (6) Stock-specific filters (ADV, beta, event day) dropped as inapplicable.
weaknesses: ADX dead zone (18-25) means no trades during extended consolidation periods — can have long flat stretches mid-session
EMA crossover signals are inherently reactive — by the time the cross fires, some of the move is already done
On expiry days, NIFTY can be erratic with both high ADX and extreme BB overshoots simultaneously — the classifier may misfire
BB reversion can fail badly during macro event-driven trending (RBI announcements, F&O expiry momentum) when ADX is slow to update

_source.original_target: MOMENTUM: 50 bps from entry; REVERSION: close crosses BB_mid
